text: Resumed from the canonical 16-entry register. Checked the charter and identified empty chronology, search, decision and run records and eight stale thread statuses.
Checked the aviation authority and Secretary’s ground-stop records, then United’s published account of impacts.
Compared the reproduced Microsoft service health incident with the university’s local status and the regulator’s account. Kept dated recovery boundaries and source provenance explicit.
Checked Microsoft’s defensive phishing disclosure and retained its limitations on confirmed credential capture and compromise.
Checked Google Security Operations and WashU’s Workday updates as separate provider or customer records.
The Jetstar incident-specific notice and payment records remain outstanding. The Melbourne university outage page was unavailable through public retrieval during this pass.
Reconciled chronology and thread views while preserving all 16 previous evidence records and all eight open questions. Evidence gathering remains open.

Incident boundaries. Dated records now distinguish aviation, Microsoft 365, the university’s Workday and Microsoft records, agriculture messaging, and Plaid’s Chase connection issue. Departmental messaging and Plaid’s publication are answered in Q-0009 and Q-0012. The freight notice is evidence of the advertised terminal plan only. Next: obtain the terminal operator’s actual downtime and bank-wide onset and restoration records.

Cause and recovery. The Microsoft report copy adds a detailed operator explanation and separates end of active impact from backlog recovery. Chase’s named spokesperson gives an attributed technical explanation. Next: check Microsoft’s authenticated publication and seek a final aviation, Workday and Chase incident report with independent support.

Malicious activity. The case has dated defensive disclosures of outage-themed phishing in 2024 and 2026. Microsoft’s 2026 disclosure reports attempted phishing and does not establish successful credential capture. Chase later reported a vendor incident, with the scope of access still unverified. Next: seek attributable affected-entity outcomes or regulator confirmation.

Outage and compromise. The service disruption records and phishing report now sit alongside attributed operator statements. No source in this pass establishes that a compromise caused one of the scoped disruptions. Next: seek incident-specific forensic findings and confirm what the scope of each defensive source actually excludes.

Dependencies and workarounds. Records identify specific reported dependencies and fallback routes, including alternative cargo lodgement, patient communications and Plaid’s Chase connection. Next: verify which fallbacks users were able to use and obtain service-level dependency records for the remaining sectors.

Consequences for people. Records now show concrete alternative steps for workers, patients and cargo clients. Q-0011 answers the university’s published patient fallback. Counts of affected people, paid reimbursements, missed appointments, payment outcomes and terminal delays remain outstanding.

Connections and separate explanations. United explicitly attributes operational impact to the ground stop. Plaid reports disruption to its connections with Chase. The cancelled agriculture maintenance windows are resolved in Q-0010 and remain distinct from the messaging disruption. Chase says it found no connection between the vendor incident and the earlier disruption. There is no evidence here tying the reported terminal plan to the other cases. Next: reconcile Microsoft D365 and Microsoft 365 product records before linking their incidents.

Uncertainty and unavailable records. The register retains the Microsoft 2024 time-zone issue, the provenance limit on the mirrored 2026 report, the distinction between service announcements and individual recovery, and the unverified Brisbane terminal operation. The Chase source’s official social post was unavailable directly in this pass. Next: obtain authenticated operator notices and dated outcome records.

Incident boundaries. Australian agriculture notices now document an actual 15 November lodgement-service disruption and a later multi-system restoration notice. Two notices on 23 November record another disruption and a separate restoration. The notices leave the separately advertised Brisbane terminal closure unverified. Brown and two healthcare trusts record local disruption or recovery, and a named passenger account adds an observed aviation consequence. Next: secure port-operator movement records and dates of recovery for affected people.

Recovery stages. The agriculture department reports service restoration at 18:40 Australian Eastern Daylight Time on 15 November without a cause. Brown reports restored Workday access while automated processing was still catching up. Next: obtain cause records and verify backlog completion at the operator and service levels.

Dependencies. The cargo lodgement route offered during the 13 November messaging disruption was itself unavailable on 15 November, after the department had issued its messaging restoration notice. On 23 November the department again reported lodgement disruption, warned of possible errors, and advised retrying failed lodgements after restoration. Brown described continued physical time-clock use for some workers. Two healthcare trusts documented distinct responses. Next: verify actual fallback use and practical access to the alternate routes.

People and recovery. The records now document a suspended self-referral route, a named passenger’s account from a grounded aircraft, and local unavailability of time reporting and other employment processes. They also give local recovery notices. Next: obtain referral wait times, payroll and transaction completion, passenger rebooking and payment outcomes, and cargo delays.

Connections. The 15 November cargo lodgement incident has a distinct date and system boundary from the 13–14 November agriculture messaging disruption. The 23 November notices document a further episode. The lodgement system’s prior fallback role is documented. Its causal relationship to the earlier disruption and to Brisbane terminal operations remains open. Next: obtain the department’s incident report and independent terminal operation records.

Evidence gaps. The new records bound the known recovery milestones and actual limits of access but do not quantify payments, missed appointments, goods delays or payroll effects. The Brisbane terminal’s actual operating status and the Microsoft time-zone discrepancy remain unresolved. Next: seek attributable operator or regulator outcome records.

The four new first-party records preserve what their publishers said about services, workarounds and limitations. Essex described an uneven return and a need to confirm urgent referrals; two ambulance services described retained emergency functions and communication contingencies. The Tasmanian parliamentary source is an uncorrected proof and attributes claims to speakers. Individual referral outcomes, actual waits, independent root cause and broader population impact remain unknown. IP Australia original retrieval failed certificate verification; no bypass or original-source claim was made.

Observer evidence 40 preserves the GitHub feed and supplies three case leads. The same retrospective post-incident explanation appears in two separately identified events and is not independent corroboration. Preserve both original creation and later modification dates. The source does not identify the upstream model provider or establish a link to Microsoft, aviation or other incidents. Original bytes are held in the local Observer archive; public descriptions are not the original source.

Compared three first-party defensive reports with the Microsoft account. Trellix reports a bounded count and later sign-in chain; Cofense describes a sign-in flow. The same sender-domain and intermediary details recur, but sample independence, actor identity, actual credential capture and outage causation remain unestablished. KnowBe4's ratios use its own three-day baseline. Originals and separate public descriptions were hashed.

The 4–5 November Australian cargo-lodgement report predates the already recorded later fallback and disruptions; no shared cause is established. The Hamilton council record reports a multi-day local service pause and later restoration while queued submissions were still being processed. CSX acquisition stopped on HTTP 403 before robots checking completed; no restriction was bypassed.

Observer evidence 41 contains five Cloudflare reports concerning Replicate inputs, model registry or predictions. Preserve each update and distinguish its creation and modification times. Separate reports on the same component do not establish a common cause, compromise, or a connection to other incidents. Public descriptions are separately hashed paraphrases; the original response remains in Observer.

The Nelson Mandela Museum attributed two extended quotation deadlines to the 13 November Microsoft system outage or technical challenge. Its notice documents an offered remedy, not the outcome for each bidder or proof of technical cause. The original PDF is retained locally with its own hash; the public description is separately hashed. Canada procurement, Royal Free London and Oxford acquisition attempts remained access gaps.

Rechecked the saved Cofense original and documented its omitted security-control claim as new evidence; the publisher account is not independent verification or proof of outage causation. Fortra could not be directly acquired after its robots check returned 403; the report itself was not requested.

Four independently captured public status pages document Anthropic and OpenAI Microsoft connectors, and separate GitHub/Codex disruptions. Preserve each displayed status update, distinguish source attribution and time precision, and do not infer a common cause. The Claude and GitHub JSON API URLs were not collected because site robots rules disallowed the requests; permitted public incident pages were captured instead.

Initial live DFAPTA pass added evidence-linked paths and cross-path analysis. Source claims retain their verification and access limits; further analysis and evidence collection remain open, and no case, evidence or analysis freeze was imposed.

Operator directed Lattice Atlas for this ongoing cyber case. Recorded 7 source-linked cross-path patterns with limits and their underlying analysis and evidence references. Evidence, analysis and atlas remain open; no common cause, exhaustive coverage or automatic continual analysis is assumed.
Added a visible correction to LAT-004: the reports use different measures, but overlap between their underlying samples is unknown. The original finding remains visible.
